sentences.text: The respondent/ Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO for short), BDA, Bengaluru, has sent this reference under Sections 30 and 31(2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (L.A. Act, 1894 for short), for apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No.46/1P measuring 3 acres situated at Thalaghattapura village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka has been acquired for the purpose of formation of further extension of Banashankari 6 th stage.
Preliminary notification has been issued on 21.11.2002.
Final notification was published in the Gazette on 10.09.2003.
The award has been passed on L.A.C. No. 136/2005 12.12.2003.
Possession of the land was taken on 03.01.2004.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.65,33,359/-.
As there was a dispute with regard to the title, the L.A.O. has sent the reference to this Court and has deposited the compensation of Rs.64,76,099/-.

The said amount has been kept in F.D. in Union Bank of India,
J.P. Nagara branch, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of this reference, the claimants have entered appearance.

.4. The General Power of Attorney holder of claimant No. 1 has filed claim statement stating that the schedule property land bearing Sy.No. 46/1 measuring 4 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas of kharab land being inherited property of claimant No. 1.

It is stated that on 10.07.1957 the claimant No. 1 sold the schedule property bearing Sy.No. 46/1 measuring 4 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas of kharab in-favour of Madareddy S/o Chinnappa through a registered sale deed.

Subsequently the claimant No. 1 had purchased schedule property bearing Sy.No. 46/1 measuring 4 L.A.C. No.
136/2005 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas from Madareddy through a registered sale deed dated 26.10.1964.
Subsequent to the registration the claimant No. 1 was in peaceful possession with respect to land bearing Sy.No. 46/1 measuring 4 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas.

The revenue authorities has transferred revenue documents in the name of claimant No. 1 vide MR No. 1/64-65.
.5.
It is stated that the claimant No. 1 had sold 1 acre out of total measuring 4 acres 19 guntas in Sy.No. 46/1 in-favour of Sushma Jain W/o S.K. Jain through registered sale deed dated 07.09.1995.

It is stated that the said Sushma Jain sold measuring 1 acre in Sy.No. 46/1 in-favour of Vijay Anand claimant No.2 through registered sale deed dated 16.08.1999; it is stated that subsequent to the purchase of land measuring 1 acre in Sy.No. 46/1 by Vijay Anand from Sushma Jain, Vijay Anand formed residential layout in land measuring 1 acre.
One B.R. Mohanram had purchased site from Vijay Anand is claimant No. 3.

Hence prayed to release the entire compensation amount along with accrued interest.
.6. In order to prove their case, General Power of Attorney holder of claimant No. 1 has been examined as PW.1.

The documents got marked at Ex.P.1 to 15.
.7.
Heard the arguments.

.8. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
 1) The claimant No.1 is  entitled for compensation  amount?
2) What order or award?

.9. My findings on the above points are:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
L.A.C. No. 136/2005 REASONS .10.
POINT No.1:
The General Power of Attorney holder of claimant No. 1 has been examined as PW.1.

He has stated that the claimant No. 1 is the absolute owner of the land bearing Sy.No. 46/1 measuring 4 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas of kharab, the schedule property being inherited property of claimant No. 1 and he has been in possession and enjoyment of the said property,
which is situated at Thalaghattapura village.
.11.

PW.1 has stated that in the year 1957 the claimant No. 1 sold the schedule property bearing Sy.No. 46/1 measuring 4 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas of kharab in-favour of Madareddy S/o Chinnappa through a registered sale deed.

Subsequently the claimant No. 1 had purchased schedule property bearing Sy.No.
46/1 measuring 4 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas from Madareddy through a registered sale deed dated 26.10.1964.
Ex.P.2 is certified copy of the said sale deed and Ex.P.2(a) is typed copy of Ex.P.2.
From the sale deed it is L.A.C. No. 136/2005 seen that claimant No. 1 had purchased Sy.No. 46/1 measuring 4 acres 15 guntas.
Ex.P.3 is an endorsement given by the Tahsildar, Bengaluru South Taluka that MR/1/64-65 in-respect of Sy.No. 46/1 is not available.
Ex.P.4 is the Form No. 16 for the period from 01.04.1960 to 31.05.1989.
The recital in document discloses that sale made by Madareddy in-favour of claimant No. 1 Lakshmanappa on 26.10.1964.
Ex..5 is the RTC Extracts (3 in number) in-respect of Sy.No. 46/1 for the period from 1979 to 1994.
In all these documents the name of Lakshmana S/o Chowdappa is mentioned in Col. No. 9 and in Col. No. 10, it is mentioned as Pitrajitha.

sentences.text: PW.1 has stated that the revenue authorities had transferred the documents in-favour of claimant No. 1 vide MR No.1/64-65 and he is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the said land.

PW.1 has stated that he has sold 1 acre out of total measuring 4 acres 19 guntas including 4 guntas of kharab in-favour of Sushma Jain under a sale deed dated 07.09.1995 as L.A.C. No. 136/2005 per Ex.P.6.
Ex.P.7 is the mutation made in pursuance to the said sale deed by the Assistant Commissioner.
Ex.P.8 is the RTC Extract.

From the RTC Extract it is seen that name of Lakshman is entered in Col. No. 9, name of Sushma Jain has been rounded of to an extent of 1 acre and name of Vijay Anand has been entered in pursuance to MR No. 12/2000-01 to an extent of 1 acre.
From the documents, it is seen that the claimant No. 1 had sold Sy.No. 46/1 to an extent of 1 acre out of 4 acres 15 guntas.
It is stated that Sushma Jain sold 1 acre in Sy.No. 46/1 in-favour of Vijay Anand under a sale deed dated 16.08.1999.
Ex.P.9 is the said sale deed.

It corroborates the evidence of PW.1.
.13.
Ex.P.10 is the mutation register extract which discloses that the sale made by Sushma Jain in- favour of Vijay Anand.
Ex.P.11 is the form No. 15 for the period from 01.06.1989 to 31.03.2004.

From the said document, it reflects the sale made by Lakshman in-favour of Sushma Jain to an extent of 1 acre on 18.09.1995 and the sale made by Sushma Jain in- L.A.C. No. 136/2005 favour of Vijay Anand under a sale deed dated 16.08.1999.
Ex.P.12 is the Aadhar card of PW.1.
Ex.P.13 is the RTC Extracts (5 in numbers) in-respect of Sy.No. 46/1 for the period from 2002 to 2006.
In the said document, name of Lakshman is mentioned in Col. No. 9 to an extent of 3 acres 15 guntas and name of Vijay Anand is mentioned to an extent of 1 acre.

Ex.P.14 is the mutation ordering to mention the extent in the khathedar column along with name of khathedar in-respect of Sy.No. 46/1 to an extent of 1 acre in- favour of Vijay Anand and 3 acres 15 guntas in-favour of Lakshman S/o Chowdappa.
.14. PW.1 has stated that Vijay Anand subsequent to purchase of 1 acre of land had formed residential layout.
PW.1 has stated that one B.R. Mohanram had purchased site from Vijay Anand who is claimant No. 3 and Vijay Anand is claimant No. 2 in the reference.

PW.1 has stated that the claimant No. 1 after selling portion of land, retained 3 acres 19 guntas which includes 4 guntas of kharab, till the land was acquired L.A.C. No. 136/2005 by the respondent authorities for formation of further extension of BSK 6th stage.
.15. PW.1 has stated that while issuing final notification 1 acre 19 guntas of land has been left out from the acquisition.

As per final notification the residential layout formed by Vijay Anand measuring 1 acre and residential site purchased by B.R. Mohanram from Vijay Anand is left out from the acquisition by the respondent authority.
PW.1 has stated that the respondent had awarded compensation in-respect of Sy.No. 46/1P and deposited the same.
The claimant No.1 being owner of the property is entitled to receive the compensation.
.16. During cross-examination PW.1 has stated that the claimant No.1 is his far relative.
The claimant No. 2 has purchased the property from claimant No.1.
The claimant No. 3 has purchased site from claimant No.2.
He admits that B.D.A. has acquired only 3 acres of land and passed the award to that extent.

He admits that the reference has been sent in respect of 2 acres 36 L.A.C. No.

sentences.text: From the oral and documentary evidence it is seen that Sy.No. 46/1 is an ancestral property of claimant No. 1 he after selling had repurchased the same.
3 acres of land has been acquired, out of which 4 guntas is unreserved kharab and L.A.O. has given compensation to the said extent of 2 acre 36 guntas plus 4 guntas of kharab.
The claimant No. 1 being owner of the said property, he is entitled to compensation.
Therefore, point No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
.18. POINT NO.2:

In view of my finding on the above point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is allowed.

Claimant No. 1 Lakshmana is entitled for compensation to an extent of L.A.C. No.
136/2005 2 acres 36 guntas plus 4 guntas of kharab in-respect of Sy.No.46/1P of Thalaghattapura village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka along with accrued interest thereon.
Claimant No. 1 has to execute indemnity bond with one surety, undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount he is going to receive in this case.
Claimant No. 1 is entitled to interest under Section 34 of the L.A. Act.
The amount already paid by L.A.O., has to be deducted.
Claim in-respect of remaining claimants is dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Judgment Writer, transcribed by her, revised by me and after corrections,
pronounced in open Court on this the 17th day of April, 2023.)
(Sheila B.M.), II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge & Spl. Judge, Bengaluru.
